s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels with plump endothelial cells
positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
lesions are firm, nonscaly, and have irregular borders
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma before lesion appearance
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
histopathological examination shows thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells are plump with no significant cytologic atypia
immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%)
immunohistochemistry negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)
